blocks.content: Igneous rocks are called primary rocks because all other rocks are formed directly or indirectly from them.

rows: Cooling and solidification of magma or lava
Weathering, deposition, and lithification of sediments
Recrystallization under high pressure and temperature
Foliated/banded texture, highly dense and hard

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: About 98% of the total crust of the earth is composed of eight major elements: oxygen, silicon, aluminium, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, and magnesium.
Feldspar and quartz are the most abundant mineral groups constituting the Earth's crust.
Igneous rocks are formed by the cooling and solidification of molten magma or lava and are known as primary rocks.
Sedimentary rocks are formed through the process of lithification, involving compaction and cementation of organic and inorganic debris.
Metamorphic rocks are created under high Temperature, Pressure, and Volume (PVT) conditions through recrystallization.
Extrusive vs Intrusive Igneous Rocks: Basalt is extrusive (fine-grained), whereas Granite is intrusive (coarse-grained).
Foliation and Banding: Frequently tested terms defined as the arrangement of mineral grains in parallel layers in metamorphic rocks.
Mohs Scale of Hardness: Talc (1) is the softest mineral, while Diamond (10) is the hardest.
Organically formed sedimentary rocks include chalk, limestone, and coal.
